etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English official, from Old French official, from Latin officiālis, from Latin officium (“duty, service”), by surface analysis, office +‎ -ial.

definitions.definition: Of or pertaining to an office or public trust.
Derived from the proper office or officer, or from the proper authority; made or communicated by virtue of authority
(Of a statement) Dubious but recognized by authorities as truth and/or canon.
(pharmaceutical) Sanctioned by the pharmacopoeia; appointed to be used in medicine; officinal.

quote.citation: 1650, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: the stomach and other parts official unto nutrition

definitions.definition: Relating to an office; especially, to a subordinate executive officer or attendant.
Relating to an ecclesiastical judge appointed by a bishop, chapter, archdeacon, etc., with charge of the spiritual jurisdiction.
An office holder, a person holding an official position in government, sports, or other organization.
